🔗 Auto-save to file Recommended — data lives in a file you own, not in Chrome

Pick a JSON file on your computer (Desktop, Dropbox, OneDrive) where the tracker will automatically save every change. If Chrome ever wipes its storage, your data is safe in the file. Re-open the tracker, point it at the file, you're back. Put the file in a cloud-synced folder for multi-computer access.

How this works:
• Click Pick file for autosave the first time — choose a location like Desktop/tcp_tracker_data.json
• Every change you make auto-saves to that file (about 1-2 seconds after you stop typing)
• When Chrome wipes its storage, just re-open the tracker and click Load existing data file — everything restores
• Requires Chrome or Edge. The old Export / Import buttons below still work as a manual backup
💾 Data backup & restore Critical: protects against data loss

Your tracker data lives in your browser's storage. If Chrome clears its data (settings, updates, switching computers) you lose everything. Export your data every week as a JSON backup file you can save anywhere. Import it later to restore.

Tips to keep data safe:
• Click Export every Monday after your meeting — save backup to Dropbox, Google Drive, or a TCP folder
• If switching computers: export from old computer, open tracker on new computer, import the file
• If Chrome wipes the data: just import your most recent backup file
• Backup file contains EVERYTHING (reps, goals, weekly data, photos, settings)
If saves are failing with “localStorage full”, click this to see what's taking up space and clear safe-to-delete items.
☁️ Cloud sync Auto-syncs every 5 min · last sync: never

This stores your FULL tracker data (same as a backup) in a private GitHub Gist. Click Save to cloud to push the latest; anyone with the token + Gist ID clicks Load from cloud to pull it. Heads up: whoever loads last sees whoever saved last \u2014 if two people save around the same time, the later save wins. Best with one clear “data owner.”

Setup once: at github.com → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens, create a token with Gist permission. Paste it above. Click Save to cloud — a private Gist is created and its ID appears in the box. Share that Gist ID (and a token with Gist access) with anyone who should pull the data.
v221+: credentials are now baked into this HTML file, so they survive browser wipes and version upgrades. Auto-sync runs every 5 min. On first load with no local data, the tracker auto-pulls from the cloud Gist.

📅 Quarter calendar (TCP fiscal weeks)

Override quarter start dates so the tracker uses TCP's actual fiscal calendar instead of standard calendar quarters. If left blank, the tracker uses default starts (Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1 walked back to the prior Sunday).

🎯 Scoring thresholds

Set the performance % thresholds for each star rating. For revenue, calls & hours: higher % = better. For art errors & credits: lower % = better (rate targets).
